subject: Automotive & EVs
title: The Backup Camera Revolution
description: A short lesson to help you apply The Backup Camera Revolution.

hook.text: Every year, hundreds of people—mostly children—were killed by drivers backing up blindly.

buildup.text: Rearview mirrors left a massive blind zone directly behind the car, especially in SUVs.

discovery.text: Small cameras on the rear bumper showed the hidden zone on a dashboard screen in real time.

twist.text: Despite clear evidence, it took over a decade of lobbying before cameras became mandatory.

climax.text: The 2018 US mandate put a rearview camera in every new car, preventing hundreds of deaths yearly.

punchline.text: A tiny camera closed the deadliest blind spot on every car.

quiz.question: When did the US mandate backup cameras in all new cars?

details.summary: Backup cameras display a live rear view on the dashboard screen when reversing, eliminating the dangerous blind zone directly behind the vehicle that mirrors alone cannot reveal.
details.whyItMatters: Backover accidents kill hundreds of people each year, many of them children. Mandatory backup cameras in new cars have reduced these tragedies by giving drivers a clear view of the area behind them.
takeaways: A rear-mounted camera feeds video to the dashboard display
Guidelines on screen show predicted path while reversing
US law has required backup cameras on all new cars since 2018

faq.question: Why were backup cameras made mandatory in the United States?
faq.answer: After years of advocacy by parents who lost children in backover accidents, the 2008 Cameron Gulbransen Kids Transportation Safety Act led to the 2018 mandate for rear cameras on all new vehicles.

faq.question: Are backup cameras better than parking sensors?
faq.answer: They serve complementary roles. Cameras show a visual image of what is behind the car, while ultrasonic sensors detect obstacles at close range and beep as a warning. Many cars now include both.
